metadata.title: Mpox: Development of Drugs and Biological Products; Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.context: Sponsors developing drugs for mpox should consider the following: 210 • To demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness, 18 development programs should 216 include randomized controlled clinical trial data in participants with mpox. The primary 217 endpoint for phase 2 or phase 3 clinical trials should be clinically meaningful and should 218 demonstrate the clinical benefit with a favorable effect on a meaningful aspect of how a 219 participant with mpox feels, functions, or survives. Sponsors should discuss appropriate 220 endpoints for phase 2 and phase 3 clinical trials with the Agency. 221

candidates.statement: • Current data indicate that mpox disproportionately affects racial and ethnic minorities, 223 who should be represented in clinical trials. 19 Sponsors should ensure that clinical trial 224 sites include geographic locations with a higher concentration of racial and ethnic 225 minorities to recruit a diverse study population. 20
candidates.context: 18 See section 505(d) of the FD&C Act and 21 CFR 314.126. Also see the draft guidance for industry Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness for Human Drug and Biological Products (December 2019). When final, this guidance will represent the FDA’s current thinking on this topic. • Current data suggest that, in the United States, approximately 40 percent of mpox cases 228 have occurred in individuals living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) 229 infection. 21 Individuals living with HIV infection should not be excluded from clinical 230 trials. 231
